answer: At dawn, an agent market assigns voting power by locked collateral, not account count. A thousand fake agents merely echo the weight of the same deposit; splitting it creates no extra influence. To gain a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more collateral than honest participants, tying up real capital. Signing conflicting votes in the same round produces a verifiable proof that burns the offender’s stake, leaving an expensive ember rather than a free identity reset.
